text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. The main idea is that developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. Each time this happens, automated builds start automatically. These builds check that the new code works together with the existing code. As part of the build, the system also runs tests. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines usually include several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. By catching issues early, teams save time and reduce stress. In short, CI helps developers work faster and with more confidence.
